Court No. - 14
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11203 of 2023

Applicant :- Rahul
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt., Lko. And Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Farhan Alam Osmany Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.Learned AGA informs that the complainant/ opposite party no.2 in this case has been sufficiently served.
In this regard the information furnished by the concerned S.H.O. has been placed for perusal by this Court and the same is taken on record.

It is also informed by learned AGA that instructions in this case along with up to date case diary has been procured, thus there appears sufficient material on the basis of which plea of bail of the applicant may be adjudicated, moreover despite the service no one has appeared on behalf of opposite party no2./ complainant.
2. Heard Shri Farhan Alam Osmany, learned counsel for the accused/applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Rahul for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 82/2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Hardoi, during trial.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication and the applicant has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

5. It is also submitted that the FIR of the instant case was lodged by the father of the victim on 15.02.2022 at Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Hardoi against the applicant and other two accused persons alleging that the applicant has enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years on 7.1.2022.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On 5.9.2022 the victim is shown to have been recovered and her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. were recorded.

6. While drawing attention of this Court towards the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., it is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix has not levelled any allegations against the applicant and had claimed that she had accompanied the applicant with her free wish, will and consent.

She also stated that they were in love with each other and have solemnized marriage in the year 2019 and she in categorical terms had stated that she had accompanied the applicant with her consent and free wish and will and she wants to live with her husband (applicant).
7.

It is also submitted that in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the victim has stated her age to be of 18 years while as per her educational credentials her age is coming as 16 years and six months while as per the ossification process the radio-logical age of the prosecutrix has been assessed as 18-19 years and in absence of any conclusive proof with regard to the basis on which the date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded in the School, her date of birth as shown in school records may not be deemed as conclusive and the prosecutrix was having sufficient intellect.

8. Learned counsel for the applicant while drawing attention of this Court towards the statement of the victim recorded before the trial court as P.W.1, extract of which has been placed on record,
submits that no allegation of any kind has been levelled by the prosecutrix against the applicant in his evidence recorded before the trial court and she has categorically stated that she had not gone with the applicant nor any physical relationship between them were established and infact she had left her home as she was annoyed by her mother.

9. It is vehemently submitted that since the prosecutrix herself has not supported the allegations as levelled in the First Information Report, the chances of conviction of the applicant before the trial court are remote.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 7.9.2022 and he is not having any criminal antecedent.
There is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
10. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that having regard to the age of the prosecutrix her consent is immaterial and the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is transpired that the prosecutrix after being recovered, in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
has not levelled any allegation against the applicant, rather she stated to have accompanied the Rahul vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74501136/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: applicant with her free wish, will and consent and also that they have solemnized the marriage in a temple in the year 2019 and they were living as husband and wife since long.
The prosecutrix was also subjected to medical examination, however, no abnormality or injury of any kind has been found on her person.

The statement of the prosecutrix has also been recorded by the trial court as P.W.1 wherein she had not levelled any allegation against the applicant and have categorically ruled out any cohabition or sexual relations between her and the applicant and it is in this background, it is submitted, that since the prosecutrix has also not stated about the establishment of sexual relations between them, the age of the prosecutrix would not be of any significance.

The age of the prosecutrix as per ossification test has been assessed as 18-19 years while as per her educational credentials she was aged about 16 years and six months at the date and time of the incident.
However, the correct age of the prosecutrix could only be determined by the trial court after providing an opportunity to the parties to led evidence in this regard.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 7.9.2022 and he is not having any criminal history.
His presence may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Rahul involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
Order Date :- 18.9.2023
